title: Haʻikū fire station awaits County Council approval
summary: On August 24, the committee recommended Bills 90 and 91 for the Haʻikū Fire Station on first reading; Bill 90 passed 6–2 with one excused. It required the parcel's remaining farm land to be used for subsistence agriculture. A resource person said he may seek a court order to delay the project, and the county's title to the site has been disputed.

boards.name: Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: The final roll call ended with six ayes, and the motion carried.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: A motion recommended Bill 91, a zoning change, on first reading.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: Bill 90 (2026), community plan amendment, recommend passage on first reading: The committee recommended Bill 90 pass on first reading.

timeline.text: One councilmember said, "I'll be voting no on this bill."
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The amendment passed with eight ayes, no noes and one excused.

timeline.text: A councilmember said staff will work with the attorneys on the wording of the subsistence agriculture condition.

timeline.text: The proposer said the requirement is a "must," not a "may."
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The committee required the parcel's remaining farm land to be used for subsistence agriculture.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The councilmember who proposed it said food is getting so expensive.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The proposer said she hopes it becomes a pilot program because the County claims ownership of a lot of farm land.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: A resource person said he may seek a court order that would delay the project.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The chair said the Board of Ethics cleared her to vote on the bills.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: Before it were Bills 89, 90 and 91 for a proposed Haʻikū Fire Station.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The fire chief said the Haʻikū fire station still needs final approval from the County Council.
timeline.body: Fire and Public Safety Commission

timeline.text: A council member said she will not support anything that dispossesses Kanaka of ancestral ʻāina (land).
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The planning department said the council can decide zoning no matter who owns the property.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The project consultant said choosing Site D, another location, would mean starting the process over.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: A resource person who said he is a native tenant argued the land patent for the site has no legal standing.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The project engineer said the water line can be moved if iwi kūpuna (burials) are suspected.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: Agriculture department staff said farming with catchment water can be done.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: Staff will send a written request asking for the capacity of the three water meters.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: Current plans show two domestic water services for the fire station and a separate fire line.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: A water department engineer said the meter list has been closed since 2013.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: A water department engineer said the fire station's meters are not expected to serve farming on the rest of the land.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The chair asked whether a meter could supply native tenant farming on the roughly 20 acres that would stay in agriculture.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The archaeology firm said it walked the whole water line route.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: A fire department staff member confirmed no federal funds are being used.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The deputy corporation counsel (county lawyer) said a title report shows the county owns the parcel free and clear.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: If the committee recommends the bills, they would go to the full council for first and second reading.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The fire chief said the project currently has no federal funding and uses only county funds.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: A testifier said the county has not followed through on consultation about burials reported on the property.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: A testifier asked the committee to pick Site D over Site B, citing land title conflicts.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The Maui Planning Commission voted to recommend approval.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The bills would change the site's agricultural designations to rural and public/quasi-public (public facility) uses.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The station would use about 6.1 acres of a 27.9-acre county-owned property.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The fire chief said the Haʻikū fire station will come to the council soon for approval after the Planning Commission approved it.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: He said the final environmental study was done in summer 2024, but his family was not contacted until October 2024.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: A resident said part of a planned Haʻikū fire station project would run through his family's kuleana (family land) parcel.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: The fire chief said the department lost a $15 million federal grant for Haʻikū Fire Station.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
